screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind study of aminophylline (theophylline analogue) vs placebo in patients with acute ischaemic stroke; randomized design is strongly implied by 'double-blind'; treatment occurred in the acute phase (3 days of infusion) consistent with within one week.

Double-blind randomized trial of intravenous aminophylline vs placebo in acute cerebral infarction; intervention delivered acutely (immediate post-injection effects) consistent with within-one-week criterion.
Open-label, single-arm dose-escalation (no randomization or control). Fails the randomized controlled trial criterion.
Population not specified as confirmed/presumed acute ischaemic stroke; design not a randomized controlled trial versus placebo/control.
Randomized cross-over physiological study in patients recovering from stroke; timing is subacute/recovery rather than within one week of onset.
Randomized cross-over physiological study focused on CBF in patients recovering from stroke; not within one week of onset.
Physiological CBF study; population not specified as acute ischaemic stroke; not a randomized trial vs placebo/control.
